headline: Hot US October CPI lifts 10-year yield toward 5 percent and Fed hike bets; Nvidia slides again
subhead: The S&P 500 fell 0.4 percent to 7,520.9 as core CPI rose 0.3 percent; Nvidia lost 5.5 percent, gold 1.7 percent and Bitcoin 2.1 percent to 73,641 dollars.

us.text: The S&P 500 fell 0.4 percent to 7,520.9 and the Nasdaq 0.7 percent after October CPI rose 0.4 percent and core 0.3 percent, both above forecasts.
Nvidia fell 5.5 percent for a second day as its board hired Wachtell Lipton to probe CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
Futures now fully price a December Fed hike, and Governor Waller backed more aggressive action; the 10-year yield briefly topped 5 percent.

india.text: Nifty edged up 0.1 percent to 25,044.7 and Bank Nifty rose 1.1 percent on Monday as IT stocks fell; markets reopen Wednesday after the Diwali break.
Foreign investors bought a net 7,212 crore rupees on Monday, a seventh straight day of buying, while domestic institutions sold 7,173 crore.
The rupee closed 5 paise firmer at 93.93 per dollar, helped by falling crude prices and foreign fund inflows.

global.text: The Kospi jumped 4.4 percent and the Nikkei 2.7 percent as chip and AI stocks rebounded, led by SK Hynix, Tokyo Electron and SoftBank.
The DAX rose 1.7 percent and the FTSE 100 1.0 percent on Monday as tech rebounded and oil fell on Iran de-escalation hopes.
WTI settled at 86.04 dollars and Brent at 91.49, lowest since late August, after Trump said he plans no new strikes on Iran during talks.

calendar.what: NSE and BSE reopen after Diwali; US Veterans Day, bond market closed; Rezera US IPO pricing expected

India October CPI, a Business Standard poll sees about 6.05 percent; US jobless claims; five Fed officials speak; Cisco, Applied Materials, Brookfield and Nebius results; Windward Bio US IPO pricing expected
US October retail sales; NVIDIA third quarter results
Anthropic IPO pricing, reported for 18 November with trading from 19 November, range 70 to 78 dollars; Microsoft and Broadcom are placement buyers

weekly.narrative: The US midterms set the tone: a relief rally on Wednesday gave way to Thursday's AI chip rout on fears a Democratic Congress curbs data center building, and Friday's partial rebound and a 165,000 payrolls beat still left the S&P 500 down 2.7 percent and the Nasdaq 3.4 percent on the week. India went the other way, with foreign buying and cheaper crude lifting the Nifty 8.6 percent on the week and above 25,000 on Friday, while Kospi and the Nikkei bore the brunt of the chip selloff. Hopes of an Iran deal drove WTI down 12.8 percent on the week, and gold rose 4.5 percent and silver 5.5 percent despite rising Fed hike bets, while Bitcoin slipped 3.4 percent. Next week brings US CPI on 10 November, India CPI on 12 November, China's rare earth export pause expiring and a reported start to Anthropic's IPO roadshow.
